result.topic_en: The page ends a question about expressing algebraic functions of several variables and maxima-minima conditions through congruences with respect to module systems, then states and begins proving a theorem that a continuous function uniformly approximated by rational functions which approximately satisfy a rational differential relation is differentiable and satisfies the differential equation F = 0.

items.quote:
Wenn eine {+stetige+} Function {+$f(x)$+} einer reellen Veränder=
lichen $x$ sich gleichmässig durch eine Reihe
rationaler Functionen $r_1(x), r_2(x), \ldots$, derart
annähern läszt, dass eine gewisse rationale
Function {+$F$+} von $f(x)$ und [-gewöhnli-] $\frac{df(x)}{dx}$
beim Einsetzen $f = r_1, r_2, \ldots$, sich gleichmäs=
sig der $0$ annähert, so ist $f(x)$ differenzir=
bar und genügt der Differentialgleichung
$F = 0$.
items.english: If a continuous function f(x) of a real variable x can be uniformly approximated by a sequence of rational functions r_1(x), r_2(x), ... in such a way that a certain rational function F of f(x) and df(x)/dx, upon substituting f = r_1, r_2, ..., uniformly approaches 0, then f(x) is differentiable and satisfies the differential equation F = 0.
